http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28273v1.summary: Balková-Pelantováの手法を用い、有限アルファベット上の右無限語 w における長さ N+1 の部分語の出現頻度（上頻度、下頻度、および存在する場合は通常の頻度）の個数について、3(p_w(N+1) - p_w(N)) + 1 以下という上界を示した。ここで p_w(n) は部分語複雑度関数である。特に、部分語複雑度が線形に抑えられている語に対しては、一様な上界が存在することを意味する。一方で、任意の弱増加関数 f(n) に対して、部分語複雑度が O(nf(n)) でありながら、長さ N の部分語の異なる頻度の個数が N→∞ において無限大となる例も提示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28273v1.appendix: 本論文は、combinatorics on words および symbolic dynamics の分野に密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28241v1.title: クリックを超えた厳密な準同型閾値
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28241v1.summary: 本論文は、ErdősとSimonovitsの問いに端を発する「彩色閾値（chromatic threshold）」およびThomassenの問いに基づく「準同型閾値（homomorphism threshold）」を扱った研究です。特定のグラフHを含まないH-freeグラフにおいて、線形な最小次数条件が有界な彩色数や有界位数のH-freeグラフへの準同型の存在をいつ強制するのかを分析しています。これまでの研究でクリック（完全グラフ）の場合の閾値は決定されていましたが、本論文ではクリック以外のより広範なグラフ族へと結果を拡張し、その族における厳密な準同型閾値を決定しました。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28241v1.appendix: 本論文は、提示された興味ある分野のうち「combinatorics on words」と同じく広義の組合せ論（極値グラフ理論）に関連する研究です。彩色数や準同型といったグラフ理論の基礎的概念の閾値決定という重要な問題に取り組んでいます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28157v1.title: 撹乱置換行列とオービット・ハーモニクス
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28157v1.summary: 本論文では、体 𝔽 上の n × n 変数多項式環 S = 𝔽[xₙₓₙ] において、撹乱置換行列（derangement permutation matrices）の軌跡 𝔇ₙ に関連するオービット・ハーモニクス商環 R(𝔇ₙ) = S/gr I(𝔇ₙ) を研究している。著者らは、消滅イデアルの随伴次数付きイデアル gr I(𝔇ₙ) の明示的な生成系を提示し、R(𝔇ₙ) のヒルベルト級数と Foata 変換および対称群 𝔖ₙ 上の最長増加部分列統計量との関係を明らかにした。さらに、R(𝔇ₙ) の次数付き 𝔖ₙ 指標に対する交代和公式を導出しており、これらの証明にはホモロジー代数における写像錐（mapping cone）の構成が活用されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28157v1.appendix: 本論文は組み合わせ論（Combinatorics）の手法を深く用いており、興味ある分野のうち combinatorics on words と数学的基礎において関連性を持ちます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28139v1.title: Anosov流における軌道の補集合の双曲性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28139v1.summary: 3次元多様体上のAnosov流が向き付け可能な安定・不安定葉層を持つ場合、充填的な周期軌道の補集合は双曲多様体となることを示した。これは双曲曲面の単位接束における閉じた充填測地線軌道の補集合に関する既知の結果を一般化したものである。また、不変葉層の向き付け可能性がこの性質に必要であることを反例の構成により示した。さらに、懸垂流の場合は任意の周期軌道集合の補集合が双曲的になり、測地流の場合は不変葉層の向き付け可能性にかかわらず、充填的かつ環状でない周期軌道集合の補集合が双曲的になることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28139v1.appendix: この論文は力学系（特にAnosov流）と多様体の幾何学（双曲幾何学）に関するものであり、指定された[興味ある分野]（symbolic dynamics, combinatorics on words等）と直接的に重なる主要テーマは明示されていませんが、Anosov流の解析においてsymbolic dynamicsの手法が背景として用いられることがあります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28138v1.title: 有限および無限盤面におけるHexの最適戦略
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28138v1.summary: 盤面ゲームHexにおける最短勝利パスの長さλ(n)と、先手勝利に必要な最小石数δ(n)の構造的性質を分析した論文。主な成果として、Campbellが2004年に提示した予想の1つであるλ(5)=7を証明した。また、無限盤面（5×∞の帯）における同様の問題ではλ(5×∞)=5となり、有限盤面よりも厳密に小さくなることを示した。これにより、有限盤面と無限盤面における最適勝利戦略の性質に根本的な違いがあることを明らかにしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28138v1.appendix: この論文は、組合せ論（combinatorics）における接続ゲームを扱っており、指定された「興味ある分野」の1つであるcombinatorics on wordsと同様に、離散構造の解析や組合せ的な最適化の性質に深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28088v1.title: クラウド型IoTアクセス制御ポリシーにおける情報フローの検証（拡張版）
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28088v1.summary: IoTクラウドプロバイダが提供するアクセス制御機構の設定ミスは、セキュリティ上の深刻な脆弱性を招く恐れがある。本研究では、AWS IoT Coreのコンポーネントを形式的にモデル化し、ポリシーによって許可されるデバイス間の通信を捉える情報フローグラフを定義した。SMTソルバを活用してこのグラフの有限表現を構築することで、デバイス間の意図しない情報フローの検証を可能にしている。提案手法をツール「IOT:POKER」として実装し、現実的なシナリオや実世界のポリシーを用いてその有効性を評価した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28088v1.appendix: 本論文は、システムの形式的モデル化やグラフ表現を通じた検証を行っており、興味ある分野のうち「automata theory」に関連する手法を基礎としています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28071v1.title: ファノ平面におけるランダムなトゥーランの定理
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28071v1.summary: ファノ平面 F（7頂点7辺の3様均一ハイパーグラフ）において、Kₙ⁽³⁾の最大F-free部分ハイパーグラフが二部グラフになるというFranklとFürediらの結果を、ランダム設定へと拡張した。本論文では、臨界値 p̂ = Θ_F ⋅ n⁻²/³ (log n)¹/⁶ を境界として、p がこれを超える場合には高確率で最大F-free部分グラフが二部グラフとなり、下回る場合には非二部グラフになるというシャープな閾値を決定した。これは、ランダムハイパーグラフにおけるトゥーラン型問題でシャープな閾値を得た初めての研究である。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28071v1.appendix: 本論文は組み合わせ論（combinatorics）における極値理論を扱っており、興味ある分野の「combinatorics on words」と関連する組み合わせ論的手法が用いられています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28001v1.title: SL₂(ℤ[1/p])の可換性に関する分類空間と中心化群
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28001v1.summary: Adem, F. Cohen, および Torres-Giese によって導入された、群 SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) における可換性に関する分類空間のホモトピー型を決定した。離散群としての構造と SL₂(ℝ) からの相対位相の両方を考慮しており、幾何学的群論の手法を用いて極大アーベル部分群（非中心元の中心化群に一致）の構造を詳細に解析している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28001v1.appendix: 本研究は、SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) という無限群の代数的・幾何的構造を扱っており、興味ある分野として挙げられた「structure of large countable infinite group」に深く関連している。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27989v1.title: フルサポートおよび切断されたサポートを持つパルチザン・サブトラクション
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27989v1.summary: 本論文では、プレイヤーごとに石を取り除ける数の上限が異なるパルチザン・サブトラクション・ゲームである「Full Support (FS)」について調査している。FSでは、移動の選択肢が多いプレイヤーが、有限個の例外を除いたほぼ全ての山のサイズで勝利することを、一般的正準形およびアトミック・ウェイトの算出を通じて示している。また、公平性を回復させるために選択肢を制限する「Truncated Support (TS)」を導入し、切断の深さが勝敗や周期性に与える影響を分析した。特定のバランスの取れた切断レベルにおいては、非自明な周期性と共に、無限のPポジションおよびNポジションが出現することが明らかになった。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27989v1.appendix: 本研究は、ゲームの周期性やポジションの配列を扱う性質上、combinatorics on words や automata theory との関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27880v1.title: マーカー性質を持たない場合の力学的次元とシフトへの埋め込み可能性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27880v1.summary: 先行研究で構築された、マーカー性質（marker property）を持たない有限平均次元力学系の例である非周期的逆極限系について調査した。この系の平均次元とMeyerovitchの力学的次元がいずれもNであることを証明した。マーカー性質を欠いているにもかかわらず、この系はアルファベット次元が3N+2の立方体シフト（cubical shift）へ等変位相埋め込みが可能であることを示した。補助的な結果として、任意のコンパクト距離化可能なアルファベット上のフルシフトの力学的次元が、その次元が無限の場合も含め、アルファベットの被覆次元に一致することを証明した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27880v1.appendix: 本論文は、記号力学系（symbolic dynamics）における埋め込み問題や次元論に関連しており、指定された興味ある分野と密接に関わっています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27753v1.title: n-color分割に対するフランクリンの等式と付随するベック型の等式
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27753v1.summary: 本論文では、通常の分割に対して成立するいくつかの古典的な等式が、n-color分割（サイズnのパーツが1, 2, ..., nのn色の色を持つことができる分割）においても正確な類似物を持つことを示しています。具体的には、パーツのサイズと色の両方がrで割り切れる異なるパーツがちょうどj個ある集合と、少なくともr回出現する異なるパーツがちょうどj個ある集合の間に成立する、n-color版のフランクリンの等式を証明しています。さらに、これに付随する2つのベック型の等式も導出しており、すべての定理に対して解析的および組合せ論的な証明の両方を与えています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27753v1.appendix: この論文は組合せ論（combinatorics）の手法を用いて分割の等式を証明しており、興味ある分野の一つである組合せ論に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27582v1.title: 良好な再帰性（nice recurrence）を持たない多項式写像とその応用
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27582v1.summary: 整数値多項式 p: ℤ → ℤ (p(0)=0) は常に良好な再帰性を持つことが知られているが、本論文では p(0)=0 を満たしながらもこの性質を持たない多項式写像 p: 𝔽₂^ω → 𝔽₂^ω の存在を示した。これにより、任意の可算無限アーベル群間の多項式写像は良好な再帰性を持つという Bergelson と McCutcheon の予想（2000年頃）を否定した。また、多項式経路に沿った交叉の大きさが次数に敏感（degree-sensitive）であることを示す力学的なメカニズムを構築した。さらに、𝔽₂^ω 値多項式に対する Furstenberg-Sarkozy 定理が、密度多項式 Hales-Jewett 予想の対称差による弱体化版と等価であることを示し、同予想の証明や反証に向けた戦略に制約を与える新たな知見を提供している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27582v1.appendix: 本論文は可算無限アーベル群の性質や構造を議論しており、提示された興味ある分野のうち「structure of large countable infinite group」に強く関連しています。また、密度多項式 Hales-Jewett 予想を扱っている点から、組合せ論的な文脈での関わりもあります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27573v1.title: 2-連結グラフの mixed metric dimension
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27573v1.summary: サイクルではない 2-連結グラフ G において、混合次元 (mixed metric dimension) は G のサイクロマチック数 c(G) の 2 倍以下であることを示した。これにより、Sedlar および Škrekovski によって提案されていた予想を肯定的に解決した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27573v1.appendix: 本論文はグラフ理論および組合せ論の分野に属しており、提示された興味ある分野の中では Combinatorics に関連します。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27552v1.title: 測定葉層構造に対する穿孔忘却写像とそのTeichmüller空間および複素力学系への応用
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27552v1.summary: 本論文では、測定葉層構造における穿孔忘却写像を導入し、写像類群、Teichmüller空間、および極値的長さとの関係を調査している。そのために、前ホモトピー的マルチカーブの立方体複体およびCAT(0)立方体複体上の樹状座標系の概念を構築した。応用として、リーマン球面上のポストクリティカル有限な有理写像の力学系において、Kevin Pilgrimが提唱した有限曲線アトラクター予想に対する部分的な結果を得ている。さらに、Teichmüller空間上の普遍曲線におけるホロ球と測地流の間の関係を明らかにしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27552v1.appendix: 本論文は[興味ある分野]のうち、complex dynamics（複素力学系）に直接関連しています。特にポストクリティカル有限な有理写像の力学系や曲線アトラクター予想を扱っています。

papers.title: Lean-verified lower bounds for the Shannon capacity of odd cycles
papers.summary: We give new lower bounds for the Shannon capacities of small odd cycles: $Θ(C_7)\geq3.258805369885\ldots$, $Θ(C_{11})\geq5.294502522149\ldots$, $Θ(C_{13})\geq6.302455083464\ldots$, $Θ(C_{15})\geq7.301600534487\ldots$, $Θ(C_{19})\geq9.357192705918\ldots$, $Θ(C_{21})\geq10.342455853338\ldots$, and $Θ(C_{23})\geq11.328224257774\ldots$. The bounds are obtained by an iterative procedure due to Gao (2026) which is based on a method by Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman (2026). The bounds are fully formalised in Lean.

papers.title: Exact-Distance Domination in Grid Graphs
papers.summary:
Let \(G_n\) be the \(n\times n\) square grid, and let \(k\geq 2\). A set \(D\subseteq V(G_n)\) is an \emph{exact-distance \(k\)-dominating set} if every vertex \(v\in V(G_n)\setminus D\) has a vertex \(u\in D\) with \(d(u,v)=k\). We write \(D_{\mathrm{opt}}^{(k)}(G_n)\) for the minimum cardinality of such a set. For every fixed \(k\), consider the limit \[ δ_k= \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{D_{\mathrm{opt}}^{(k)}(G_n)}{n^2}. \]
  We prove that, for every fixed \(k\geq 3\), \[ \frac{1}{4k} \leq δ_k \leq \frac{k-1}{3k^2-k-1}. \] For \(k=2\), the lower and upper bounds coincide asymptotically, giving \(δ_2=1/9\).

papers.title: On the number of $g$-dimonoids of small order
papers.summary: We study $g$-dimonoids, that is, algebraic structures endowed with two associative binary operations satisfying a specified system of axioms. The paper investigates duality and isomor\-phisms of $g$-dimonoids and provides a complete characterization of all rectangular commuta\-tive $g$-dimonoids. Several new examples are constructed, including commutative iso-dual $g$-dimonoids that are not abelian, and noncommutative nonabelian rectangular $g$-dimonoids that are not dimonoids. A complete classification of all two-element $g$-dimonoids is obtained. Finally, we present the results of computer computations determining the numbers of all pairwise non\-isomorphic $g$-dimonoids of orders up to~$5$, as well as all pairwise nonisomorphic commutative, abelian, and rectangular $g$-dimonoids of orders up to~$6$, obtained using \texttt{GAP}, \texttt{Python}, and \texttt{C++}.

papers.title: A minimum-degree threshold for colour-biased Hamilton cycles in hypergraphs
papers.summary: We determine the asymptotically best possible minimum vertex degree condition forcing a two-coloured $3$-graph to contain a colour-biased tight Hamilton cycle. This confirms a conjecture of Hàn, Lang, Marciano, Pavez-Signé, Sanhueza-Matamala, Treglown and Zárate-Guerén.

papers.title: Lattice walks, pattern statistics, and Riordan arrays
papers.summary: We introduce a new class of Riordan matrices corresponding to lattice walks with colored steps. We show that this class corresponds to a class of pseudo-involutions and then find both generating functions and explicit combinatorial formulas for entries of these Riordan matrices. We use these Riordan matrices to find an explicit combinatorial formula for the occurences of an arbitrary pattern in our lattice walks. Finally, we define a distributive lattice on our lattice walks and connect our new RNA matrices to Whitney numbers of lattices.

papers.title: Bipartite Extremal Numbers of Trees
papers.summary: We study a restriction of the classical Erdős--Sós problem, the extremal number of trees, to the class of bipartite host graphs, both when only the order of the host is prescribed and when its two part-sizes are fixed. We give natural lower-bound constructions and formulate corresponding linear upper-bound conjectures. We apply a weighted variant of $k$-minimality to prove upper bounds for a broad family of trees including brooms, trees with part-sizes differing by at most one, and all trees on at most 7 vertices, resolving part of a problem of Caro, Patkós and Tuza up to additive constants. We also relate the fixed-part extremal number of a tree to the ordinary extremal number, and consider an oriented bipartite extremal function analogous to the Zarankiewicz function.

papers.title: Strongly converging unitary representations for extensions by exact groups
papers.summary: We prove the existence of strongly converging unitary representations in various new settings of countable groups, in particular, arising as extensions by exact groups: semidirect products with amenable groups; generalized wreath products with abelian base; graph wreath products; various free-by-cyclic groups including Gersten's group; and general Bernoulli shift crossed products on $C^*$-algebras.

papers.title: On some perfect matching conjectures in infinite, cubic, bridgeless graphs
papers.summary: The Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture states that every bridgeless cubic graph has six perfect matchings such that each edge belongs to exactly two of them. This conjecture has remained open since 1971, and several of its weakenings have been proposed over the years. Two of the most prominent are the Fan-Raspaud Conjecture and the Máčajová-Škoviera Conjecture. It is well known that the Berge-Fulkerson Conjecture implies the Fan-Raspaud Conjecture, which in turn implies the Máčajová-Škoviera Conjecture. These problems have been studied for years in the context of finite graphs, and many equivalences between them and other results have been established. However, little to nothing is known about them in the context of infinite graphs. In this paper, we investigate whether these conjectures remain valid in the infinite setting, establish their implications in analogy to the finite case, and prove that their finite versions are equivalent to their respective infinite versions.

papers.title: Transcript-Managed Transformers: Monotone Multi-Agent Collapse and Universality with Two Pop-Enabled Transcripts
papers.summary:
We study transcript management for fixed, finite-precision causal Transformers. A transcript is partitioned into channels of bounded blocks. Each transition consults a fixed visible suffix and may append one block, leaving the model, weights, and token protocol unchanged. The operation $P_c:=\PopContext(c)$ deletes the newest block on channel $c$ and exposes its predecessor.
  We model the layer by the Transcript-Managed Transducer $\TMTn{k}$: one finite controller, $k$ channels, and per-round actions from stay, push, and pop under a caller-driven status map. Fixed visible windows encode as finite symbols. The pop-free Restricted Transcript-Managed Transducer $\RTMTn{k}$ is the standard append-only layer and, for every fixed $k$, realizes exactly the deterministic finite-state transductions. The same holds for every fixed finite agent population under a monotone protocol that appends, routes, and copies visible blocks.
  Admitting $\{P_c\}_{c=1}^k$ restores pop. Newest-first, a pop-enabled channel is a stack; compiling to the Hopcroft--Ullman presentation transfers the classical hierarchy: $\DCFL$ for $k=1$ and $\RE$ for every $k\ge2$. Orchestrated one-channel agents match one controller with $k$ channels, so two pop-enabled transcripts---in one agent or two---suffice for universality. Simulation costs and invariance to fixed block size and visible radius are stated. The bounds fix precision, alphabets, blocks, visibility, controller state, and population; growing exact context, hidden-block access, writable stores, and unbounded \textbf{Spawn} add further state.

papers.title: Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees
papers.summary:
The $q$-state ferromagnetic Potts model on a graph $G$ is a probability distribution on all $q$-colourings of $G$ that favours many monochromatic edges. Approximate sampling from the Potts model is a central problem in the study of spin systems on sparse graphs, especially in the low-temperature regime, where the model strongly favours ordered configurations, often creating bottlenecks that make Markov-chain sampling inefficient or difficult to analyse.
  We focus on the sparse random graph $G(n,d/n)$. The local neighbourhoods of $G(n,d/n)$ are tree-like, but the relevant underlying graph is a Poisson Galton-Watson tree. This motivates the study of Glauber dynamics for the low-temperature Potts model on such trees with monochromatic boundary conditions. The Poisson setting introduces difficulties absent from the regular case: degrees fluctuate, long induced paths may appear, and branches can terminate before reaching the boundary. As a result, the effect of the monochromatic boundary at the leaves is much less uniform.
  Our main result shows near-linear mixing for the Glauber dynamics on Poisson trees with monochromatic boundary conditions. This extends the corresponding regular-tree results of Martinelli, Sinclair, and Weitz (SODA 2004) and of Blanca, Chen, Stefankovič, and Vigoda (RANDOM 2021) to the irregular trees arising from sparse random graphs. Our proof introduces an adaptive block decomposition of the tree, built around regions containing large regular subtrees, and combines it with correlation-decay estimates and functional-inequality arguments.
  We also obtain a near-linear-time approximate sampling algorithm for the Potts model on $G(n,d/n)$ at all temperatures, speeding up the best previous algorithm of Galanis, Goldberg, and Smolarova (ICALP 2025). The main new ingredient is a refined analysis of the low-temperature regime, building on the Poisson tree result.

papers.title: Slice and Partition Rank Criteria for Polynomial Zero-Avoidance
papers.summary:
We study polynomial zero-avoidance over finite vector spaces by means of slice rank and partition rank. We first make the support-entropy method effective by showing how a finite dual certificate yields an explicit entropy gap whenever the coefficient support admits no probability distribution with uniform marginals. For the quadratic elementary symmetric polynomial over fields of characteristic three, the ternary structure of the coefficient support gives a certificate with optimal normalized margin and a uniform analytic bound for the corresponding higher-degree Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv constant, avoiding a separate optimization for each field.
  We then use partition rank to handle solutions in pairwise distinct variables. Equality profiles are encoded by contracted local tensors, reducing the global problem to finitely many slice-rank estimates. Applying this reduction on the multiplicative torus gives restricted-alphabet zero-sum bounds with exponential base below the alphabet size. Coordinatewise inversion and support stratification then yield, to the best of our knowledge, the first nontrivial exponential bound for the higher-degree Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv problem over $\mathbb{F}_5^n$ associated with the fourth elementary symmetric polynomial.

papers.title: Edge-Span Chern Algebras of Graphical Configuration Spaces
papers.summary: Place the vertices of a finite graph at projective points. Each edge defines a span map to $\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$; the pulled-back Chern classes generate a graded algebra $A_G^{(n)}$. This assignment is a covariant graph functor, so the abstract graded-algebra type is a graph invariant. In ambient dimension four, the Hilbert series is incomparable with the chromatic and Tutte polynomials. On five vertices in dimension three, the $34$ graph classes yield $33$ algebra types, strictly refining both classical polynomials. For every tree $T$, we obtain a closed Hilbert-series formula depending only on $|V(T)|$ and $n$, while $A_T^{(3)}$ determines $T$ up to isomorphism. More precisely, its cubic relation data is a complete tree invariant of polynomial size. Finally, the graphical configuration space embeds as a dense open in the picture variety, and picture spaces with equal additive homology can have nonisomorphic edge-Chern algebras.

papers.title: The Basilica group of the Grigorchuk-Erschler group
papers.summary: Francoeur and Garrido recently provided the first explicit examples of finitely generated branch groups with maximal subgroups of infinite index, where one of their examples is the Grigorchuk-Erschler group. Here, using the Basilica operation constructed by Petschick and Rajeev, we show that the second Basilica group of the Grigorchuk-Erschler group also has maximal subgroups of infinite index.

papers.title: Decomposition-based Energy-based Dual-Phase Dynamics Identification for Nonlinear MDOF Systems
papers.summary: System identification is an important step in modeling and evaluating vibrating structures, but many nonlinear system identification methods rely heavily on data-driven approaches that may not preserve physical consistency. This research extends the Energy-based Dual-phase Dynamics Identification (EDDI) method to multiple-degree-of-freedom (MDOF) mechanical structures undergoing nonlinear vibrations. The original EDDI framework was designed for single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) systems and operates in two phases: the first identifies a model for internal nonconservative force, and the second captures internal conservative force. However, EDDI assumes that the potential energy is zero whenever the displacement is zero. For MDOF systems, this assumption requires all degrees of freedom (DOFs) to achieve zero displacement simultaneously, which simply occurs too infrequently in multimodal responses for direct application. To overcome this limitation, this work introduces Decomposition-based EDDI, which applies EDDI to decomposed response components to enable nonlinear system identification of MDOF systems. Wavelet-Bounded Empirical Mode Decomposition is used to extract nearly orthogonal, monochromatic intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) from the measured displacements. Each IMF is then treated as an individual SDOF oscillator and processed using EDDI to estimate its nonconservative and conservative internal forces. The IMF forces are then summed to reconstruct the total nonconservative and conservative forces acting on each physical DOF, which are used to identify the damping and stiffness models, respectively. The proposed EDDI framework is experimentally validated on a two-story tower structure with strong stiffness nonlinearity coupling the two floors. The results demonstrate the efficacy of EDDI in isolating and identifying complex, multi-modal nonlinear structural dynamics.

papers.title: Strong invariants and Tverberg numbers in convexity spaces
papers.summary:
Helly, Carathéodory, and Radon numbers encode three kinds of finite certificates in a convexity space: for the emptiness of an intersection, for membership in a convex hull, and for the existence of intersecting hulls. We study exact versions of these certificates, in which a subfamily must preserve the whole intersection or a subset must preserve the whole hull. Our first main result shows that, for finite configurations in an arbitrary convexity space, five a priori different boundedness conditions are equivalent: VC-dimension, strong Helly number, strong Carathéodory number, comatching number, and strong Radon number (with the expected additive-one shift). We also obtain equivalent layered Tverberg-type decompositions and colorful consequences.
  The common mechanism is exposed by the bipartite incidence graph between points and a generating family. For finite spaces, the unique minimal generator yields a natural dual convexity space; we characterize double dualization and prove that the strong parameters are duality invariant. The same model gives a polynomial-size, $O(t^4)$, realization of Bukh's counterexample to the Calder-Eckhoff partition conjecture.
  Finally, we obtain the first Tverberg bound for separable convexity spaces that is simultaneously linear in the number of parts and polynomial in the Radon number. If an $S_3$-separable convexity space has Helly number $h$ and its halfspaces have VC-dimension $d$, then $r_t=O(dh\log h)\,t$; in particular, Radon number $r$ gives $r_t=O(r^2\log r)\,t$. The bound attains the weak-Eckhoff scale $O(rt)$ whenever the Helly number is bounded. For axis-parallel box convexity in $\mathbb{R}^k$, gives the optimal order $r_t=O(rt)$ uniformly in every dimension. This appears to be the first dimension-uniform estimate of weak-Eckhoff order for box convexity, whereas the previous direct theory was confined to dimension three.

papers.title: Exponential mixing via invariant foliations and relatively Anosov homeomorphisms
papers.summary: We prove that every closed manifold of dimension $n\ge 4$ which admits a singular $2$-foliation (a foliation by closed surfaces whose quotient is a punctured $(n-2)$-torus) supports a volume-preserving homeomorphism with exponential decay of correlations for Hölder observables. The proof introduces a class of systems called relatively Anosov homeomorphisms, which fails differentiability only at the singular set. We apply a general dichotomy that bounds the decay of correlations of any homeomorphism preserving an invariant foliation by the maximum of the decay rates of the quotient dynamics and of the leafwise cycles. This dichotomy is of independent interest and yields, as immediate consequences, decay rates for product systems, skew products, partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with compact center leaves, finite covers, and extensions by expanding fibre maps. We then prove this gives a positive answer to a conjecture of Dolgopyat and Pesin regarding the realization problem for exponential decay of correlations over a large class of manifolds for which there were no known systems with exponential decay of correlations. In particular, we construct infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic closed $4$-manifolds which admit a volume-preserving homeomorphism with exponential decay of correlations, albeit not supporting either Anosov diffeomorphisms or strong partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: Rational Jacobi Rotations and the Complexity of Approximating Mixed Integer Quadratic Programming
papers.summary: We present an algorithm that finds an epsilon-approximate solution to a mixed integer quadratic programming (MIQP) problem, and that runs on a Turing machine in time polynomial in the size of the instance and in 1/epsilon, provided that the number of integer variables and the number of negative eigenvalues of the Hessian of the objective function are fixed. Unless P=NP, both restrictions are necessary, so this completes the characterization of the complexity of approximating MIQP in terms of the number of integer variables and the inertia of the Hessian; the result is new already in the purely continuous case. The main ingredient is a polynomial-time simultaneous diagonalization algorithm: it computes a rational change of basis that maps a given ellipsoid, presented in factored form, exactly to a ball, while making the objective function separable up to an arbitrarily small perturbation and preserving the inertia of its Hessian. The classical construction, in which the objective function is made exactly separable, requires a change of basis that is in general irrational, and cannot be carried out on a Turing machine; ours rests instead on rational Jacobi rotations, which we believe to be of independent interest.

papers.title: Automatic Enumeration of Tilings by Polyominoes
papers.summary: We revisit Zeilberger's computational framework for enumerating polyomino tilings and demonstrate its use in counting tilings of $k\times n$ boards by $L$-tetrominoes, allowing rotations. Recently, Bělohoubek and Slavík gave a generating function for tilings of $2n\times 4$ boards by $L$-tetrominoes. Motivated by their work, we first verify the method by automatically recovering their generating function. We then apply the method to widths $5$ through $9$ and obtain explicit rational generating functions and new integer sequences that are not currently listed in the OEIS.

papers.title: Structure of 2-step nilpotent ergodic averages for distinct-degree polynomials
papers.summary: We investigate manifestations of the Nilpotent Heuristic, which posits that recurrence and convergence phenomena known for measure-preserving $\mathbb{Z}^D$-systems extend to nilpotent group actions. Our main results establish seminorm estimates and limiting formulas for multiple ergodic averages arising from actions of 2-step nilpotent groups. In particular, if $T_1,\ldots,T_\ell$ are totally ergodic and generate a 2-step nilpotent group, then \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N T_1^n f_1 \cdots T_\ell^{n^\ell}f_\ell = \prod_{j=1}^{\ell}\int f_j\,dμ\] in the $L^{2}$ norm for all bounded functions $f_{1},\dots,f_{\ell}$; the same holds for any distinct-degree polynomial iterates. We also obtain popular-common-difference versions of the polynomial Szemeédi theorem in the same setting. In a different direction, our approach allows us to completely resolve the joint ergodicity conjecture for multidimensional polynomials and $\mathbb Z^D$-systems; we also present an example showing that, surprisingly enough, the 2-step nilpotent analog fails. We conclude with many open problems concerning joint ergodicity, seminorm estimates, and the structure theory of nilpotent systems.

papers.title: Monochromatic cycle partitions in 3-mean edge-colourings
papers.summary: Given $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and an edge-coloured complete graph such that the average number of colours incident with a vertex is at most $r$, Conlon and Stein asked whether there is a vertex partition into a bounded number of monochromatic cycles, and proved this for $r=2$. We settle the first open case by proving the corresponding statement for $r=3$.

papers.title: Precise asymptotics at the tip of the Mandelbrot set
papers.summary:
For the quadratic family $f_c(z)=z^2+c$, the only parameters in the Mandelbrot set $\cal M$ for which the Julia set $\cal J_c$ has Hausdorff dimension $1$ are $c=0$ and $c=-2$.
  Near $c=0$, Ruelle's theory gives a real-analytic expansion of the dimension.
  The tip $c=-2$ of $\cal M$, however, is a non-hyperbolic parameter and the dimension function $c\mapsto \mathrm{dim_H}(\cal J_c)$ is highly discontinuous there. We prove the sharp first-order asymptotic for the lower envelope of the Hausdorff dimension at the tip: If $c\in \cal M $ then $\mathrm{dim_H}(\cal J_c)$ lies asymptotically above $1+ Ω\sqrt{|c+2|}$ with the Jaksztas constant $Ω=\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\frac{1}{π\log 2}$. This is a surprisingly precise contribution to the Yoccoz problem about unfolding attractors.
  The proof develops a thermodynamic formalism for degenerating families of box mappings. At each scale, for parameters $c\to -2$, the induced dynamics exhibit a uniform property of exponential tails, generating improved control of their pressure functions.

papers.title: Structural Classification of a Graph with Independence Number Five
papers.summary: The independence polynomial of a simple graph $G$ is given by \( I_G(z) = i_0 + i_1 z + i_2 z^2 + \cdots + i_αz^α\), where \( i_α\) denotes the size of a maximum independent set, also called the independence number of the graph. The independence polynomial has the notable feature of being essentially closed under graph composition (lexicographic product). In this paper, we determine the independence polynomials of size five. For a disconnected graph $G$, we exploit the fact that $I_G(z)$ factors as the product of the independence polynomials of the connected components of $G$. Furthermore, we classify all independence polynomials that can occur for such a disconnected graph $G$ and, by examining their component structures, we characterize the disconnected configurations that may arise.

papers.title: Chebyshev Recurrence Structures for Reduced Spectral Functions of Cyclic Circulant Graphs
papers.summary: Let $S$ be a nonempty finite set of positive integers, let $q=\max S$, and let $B_n(S)$, $n>2q$, be the normalized product sequence associated with the Chebyshev-type polynomial of the cyclic circulant graph $G_n(S)$. When $G_n(S)$ is connected, $B_n(S)$ is both the normalized spanning-tree number and a normalized special value of the \emph{reduced spectral function}, a determinant-type function constructed from the non-trivial adjacency spectrum. Chebyshev root representations and the existence of linear recurrences for fixed-step circulant spanning-tree sequences are known. Starting from these representations, we explicitly construct a monic annihilating polynomial $\mathcal H_S(X)\in\mathbb Z[X]$ of degree $3^{q-1}$, which yields a general upper bound for the recurrence order of $B_n(S)$. By collecting coincident exponential bases and accounting for possible cancellations, we determine the minimal annihilating polynomial and give a sufficient condition under which the minimal recurrence order is exactly $3^{q-1}$. For $S=\{1,2,3\}$ and $S=\{1,3\}$, we explicitly derive the corresponding ninth-degree annihilating polynomials and prove their minimality.

papers.title: Spectral theory of frame flows on closed hyperbolic manifolds
papers.summary: We prove a resolvent estimate for the generator of the frame flow on hyperbolic manifolds away from vertical lines of resonances. A byproduct of the proof is an optimal essential spectral gap property for the generator, hence giving another proof of exponential mixing of frame flows with respect to the volume measure of the frame bundle. This extends the result of [https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08387v2] in dimension 3 to any dimension. We make an extensive use of the Borel-Weil calculus developed in [https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14846] to overcome difficulties of this higher-dimensional case.

papers.title: SAT Certificates for the Matrix-Multiplication Challenges over F2: All Ten `Expected-UNSAT` Instances Are Satisfiable, and a Type-3-Free Rank-23 Scheme
papers.summary: The matrix-multiplication SAT benchmark of Heule, Kauers, and Seidl asks, among other tasks, for solutions of ten known-satisfiable rank-23 formulas, proofs of unsatisfiability for ten formulas expected to be unsatisfiable, and a rank-23 scheme over $\mathbb{F}_2$ having a summand with no type-3 monomial. We give complete satisfying assignments for the 21 CNFs in the repository's top-level challenge1/, challenge2/, and challenge3/ directories at commit 150b2e2f. The principal finding is that all ten top-level Challenge-2 formulas are satisfiable. A direct audit shows that their hardcoded type-3 pairings are imposed by positive unit clauses on the 621 base variables: the formulas require selected incidences but do not forbid additional type-3 incidences. Starting from exact 23-summand schemes, we use the $\mathrm{GL}(3,2)^3$ isotropy action, cyclic trace symmetry, and perfect matching of transformed summands to constrained slots to construct witnesses for all ten files. For Challenge 3, we combine a locked semantic repair with a two-term identity over $\mathbb{F}_2$ to obtain a distinguished summand of type-3 count zero. Every semantic decomposition has zero residual in all 729 Brent equations. The accompanying DIMACS models assign all 26,541 variables of each formula and satisfy all 2,461,316 clauses across the 21 instances. A separate parser and clause evaluator rechecks the emitted models. A deterministic one-file Python reproducer regenerates the 21 certificates from the original CNFs in approximately nine seconds on the reported test host.

papers.title: On the spectral analysis of dynamical Möbius-Sarnak process and topological entropy of Möbius fonction
papers.summary: By extending the Rokhlin-Sinai machinery relating to the entropy and countable Lebesgue component in the spectrum, we establish that the dynamical Möbius-Sarnak process has a countable Lebesgue component. Inspired by recent work of M. Lin and the author, we extend the notion of spectral measure to all operators on Banach spaces. This generalization is further motivated by the Bellow-Losert extension of Wiener's notion of the spectral measure of sequences. Furthermore, we establish unconditionally that the topological entropy of the Möbius flow is given by $\frac{6}{π^2}\log 3$. Among other consequences, we recover a recent result by el Abdalaoui-Nerurkar which asserts that for any quasi-generic measure for the Möbius function, the Möbius flow equipped with this measure has a countable Lebesgue component in its spectrum. It follows that the Sarnak Möbius orthogonality conjecture holds for any topological dynamical system with singular spectrum. We further show that all the potential spectral measures of he Möbius function are absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: Temporal Role Colouring
papers.summary: A role colouring of a graph $G$ is an assignment of colours to the vertices of $G$ such that two vertices of the same colour have identical sets of colours in their neighbourhoods. This model is used to capture the idea of vertices having roles in a contact network, consistent with the set of roles of their contacts. We define an extension of the role colouring problem to temporal graphs. Temporal roles are defined via an automaton with states and transitions capturing both the current colour of a vertex and information about its current and past adjacencies. We show, by a reduction from the static problem, that the temporal role colouring problem is NP-complete. To contend with this intractability, we explore several parameterisations. We give fixed-parameter tractability results with respect to the number of states of the automaton combined with either the vertex-interval-membership width or the tree-interval-membership width of the temporal graph. We further show the problem is in FPT parameterised by the treewidth of the underlying graph, the lifetime of the temporal graph and the number of colours combined.

papers.title: About two results for new valid juggling sequences
papers.summary: In this note, we study two simple operations for extending juggling (siteswap) sequences, called first throws and last catches. Both constructions come from a natural question for a juggler: how can one add throws at the beginning or catches at the end of a pattern without creating a collision? Using landing times and the permutation test, we give necessary and sufficient conditions under which these constructions, when applied to an arbitrary valid siteswap, produce another valid siteswap. We complement our analysis with several examples. An interactive visualization of these extensions is available in [Para].

papers.title: Enumeration and Classification of Triangle-Maximal Pseudoline Arrangements
papers.summary:
We describe algorithms for the exhaustive enumeration and classification of simple arrangements of $n$ pseudolines ($n$ odd) maximizing the number of triangular faces. The depth-first search enumerates reduced words for the longest permutation $w_0$ by branching only on the even-indexed generators, using pruning constraints imposed by the geometry of optimal arrangements. The approach handles both perfect arrangements with a regular triangular pattern and unavoidable deviations from it for $n \equiv 1 \pmod 6$.
  The output is classified into a hierarchy of equivalence classes: by commutation, by Euclidean transformations, and by projective transformations. For each projective class we recover its full symmetry group $G \subseteq S_{n+1}$ together with the orbit-stabilizer profile of its Euclidean subclasses. Completeness of the search and classification is proved: every wiring diagram is reached.
  We report full enumerations; e.g. for $n=27$, 85,562,064 wiring diagrams partitioned into 56,646 projective classes. For larger $n$ (up to $n=93$), where exhaustive enumeration is out of reach, we report partial (first-hit) results.

papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Symbolic Dynamics: A Textile Framework For 3-graphs
papers.summary: Textile systems are best known to model two-dimensional shifts of finite type. In this article, we associate a discrete algebra with a textile system and provide a groupoid model for it. When the textile system is left-resolving, this algebra coincides with the Kumjian--Pask algebra of the associated $2$-graph. The main objective of this paper is to extend textile systems to dimension $3$ so that the resulting structures can, on the one hand, capture all three-dimensional shifts of finite type and, on the other hand, provide a textile-like framework for $3$-graphs extending the well-known connection between $2$-graphs and left-resolving textile systems. We introduce a model of a three-dimensional textile system and investigate the interplay between such textile systems and $3$-graphs. In particular, our investigation shows that the conditions required to form a $3$-graph from a $3$-colored graph (including the delicate associativity condition on tricolored paths), can be encoded in terms of simple pullback diagrams arising from the textile data. We also define homology groups for three-dimensional textiles and prove that these groups coincide with the homology groups of the associated $3$-graphs, thus establishing that our construction is homologically consistent with $3$-graphs.

papers.title: Quasilinear normal form for the Kirchhoff-Poho{\v z}aev equation
papers.summary:
On the $n$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^n$, we consider the Kirchhoff-Poho{\v z}aev equation, which is the only Kirchhoff-type equation known to admit global
  solutions for small initial data in $H^s \times H^{s-1}$, $s \geq 2$.
  We study this equation from a dynamical perspective by means of a quasilinear
  normal form approach. We perform two steps of normal form reduction and show
  that the resulting cubic and quintic terms do not contribute to the Sobolev
  energy estimates. This cancellation reveals a special algebraic structure of the
  equation and represents a first step towards a dynamical explanation of its
  exceptional global well-posedness. As a further consequence, we obtain improved
  bounds on the growth of Sobolev norms and improved lower bounds on the existence
  time for initial data in $H^s \times H^{s-1}$ with $s \in [3/2, 2)$.

papers.title: Root-of-unity weighted trigonometric power sums: a constant term approach
papers.summary: We present a unified method for evaluating finite sums of powers of cotangent, tangent, cosecant and secant weighted by primitive $k$th roots of unity. The approach relies on constant term extraction for iterated Laurent series, combined with generating functions and partial fraction decomposition. We obtain explicit closed-form expressions for all even-power sums of the four functions, as well as for odd-power cotangent and tangent sums. The formulas are given in terms of Bernoulli polynomials, Euler polynomials, and universal coefficients $r_{n,t}$. As applications, we recover numerous classical identities---including the ordinary and alternating cotangent power sums and Acton's alternating tangent sum---in a systematic and elementary way.

papers.title: On the $2$-dimensional flow number of the Flower snarks
papers.summary:
Let $r\ge 2$ be a real number, $d$ a positive integer. A $d$-dimensional nowhere-zero $r$-flow, or $(r,d)$-NZF, on a graph $G$ is an orientation of $G$ together with a function $f\colon E(G)\to \mathbb{R}^d$, such that for all $e\in E(G)$, the Euclidean norm of $f(e)$ lies in the interval $[1,r-1]$, and for every $v\in V(G)$ the sum of all incoming flow values at $v$ equals the sum of all outgoing ones. The $d$-dimensional flow number of $G$ is the parameter $φ_d(G)=\inf \{r\colon G$ has an $(r,d)$-NZF$\}$.
  In this paper we provide a lower bound for the $2$-dimensional flow number of the the Flower snark. In particular, together with a previous numerical result by the authors, we prove that $φ_2(J_n) \in [1 + 2 \sin\frac{5}{22}π, 2.387893647]$, where $J_n$ denotes the Flower snark on $4n$ vertices.

papers.title: Fitting's Theorem and Semirings of Normal Subgroups
papers.summary: We define a non-unital, generally non-associative, commutative semiring structure on the collection of normal subgroups of a group $G$. This viewpoint allows us to recast in ring-theoretic terms Fitting's classical theorem that the join of two nilpotent normal subgroups is nilpotent. From this perspective, the two key inputs are a binomial expansion in a non-associative setting and the fact that the commutator subgroup of two normal subgroups lies in each factor. The development is formalized in Lean, making essential use of Mathlib for the core definitions and results.

papers.title: The N-Prime Graph Question is equivalent to the Prime Graph Question
papers.summary:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $V(\mathbb ZG)$ be the group of normalized units of its integral group ring. We prove that every $N$-prime arc of $V(\mathbb ZG)$ either already occurs in $G$ or admits commuting witnesses of distinct prime orders. Writing $A(Δ)$ for the arc set of a directed graph $Δ$, $E(Δ)$ for the edge set of an undirected graph, and $\operatorname{Sym}(E)$ for the two orientations of the edges in $E$, this is equivalent to the exact formula \[ A\bigl(Γ_{\mathrm N}(V(\mathbb ZG))\bigr) =
A\bigl(Γ_{\mathrm N}(G)\bigr) \cup \operatorname{Sym}\!\bigl( E(Γ_{\mathrm{GK}}(V(\mathbb ZG))) \bigr). \] Consequently, the $N$-Prime Graph Question has an affirmative answer for $G$ if and only if the Prime Graph Question does.

papers.title: Learning Lookahead Lemmas for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: State-of-the-art neural network verifiers use the branch-and-bound procedure as their core solving mechanism. We introduce an inprocessing framework for neural network verification driven by the lookahead procedure. Under this framework, lookahead derives new lemmas over the phases of unstable ReLUs, which are collected into an implication graph that is used to prune the search space and vivify boolean cuts. We instantiate the framework in two state-of-the-art verifiers, Marabou and $α$-$β$-CROWN, and demonstrate that it improves performance in both, proving up to 34% more instances unsatisfiable.

papers.title: The Entropic Sum-Product Phenomenon
papers.summary:
Let $X,X'$ be independent and identically distributed discrete real-valued random variables of finite Shannon entropy, and write $H(X)$ for the Shannon entropy of $X$. We prove that \[
  \max\{H(X+X'),\,H(XX')\} \ge \frac87 H(X)-O(\log H(X)). \] This is the entropic analog of the celebrated sum-product phenomenon, and answers a question of Goh, which simply asked for a coefficient strictly larger than 1. An example by the author, Gavalakis, and Kontoyiannis showed the coefficient cannot exceed $\frac43$. Previous work by Gavalakis, Goh, and Kontoyiannis was able to prove a result of a weaker form, which could not translate to a coefficient strictly larger than 1 because of examples where the min-entropy is significantly smaller than the Shannon entropy. By splitting the distribution of $X$ into uniform pieces, which costs $O(\log H(X))$ entropy, we obviate this issue, establishing a coefficient of $\frac{10}{9}$. We augment this to $\frac87$ by adapting the work of Solymosi, which established the combinatorial sum-product phenomenon with coefficient $\frac43$ by bounding the multiplicative energy, to the entropy setting, again via a uniformization technique.

papers.title: Dynamics-aware identification of governing equations from sparse and noisy data
papers.summary: Sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) and PDE functional identification (PDE-FIND) recover parsimonious ordinary and partial differential equations (ODEs and PDEs) from data. However, sparse and noisy temporal measurements can make derivative estimates unreliable. To address this problem, we evaluate Koopman-based upsampling techniques implemented with dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), extended DMD (EDMD), and optimized DMD. These methods learn finite-dimensional approximations of Koopman evolution on selected observables and are used to interpolate and denoise snapshots inside the observed time window before derivative estimation and sparse regression. The empirical benchmark comprises two ODE systems, Lorenz-63 and Van der Pol, and three periodic PDE systems, Burgers, Fisher-Kolmogorov-Petrovskii-Piskunov (Fisher-KPP), and linear advection-diffusion, over sparse and noisy sampling regimes. Polynomial EDMD gives the strongest ODE results, especially in coefficient accuracy. The PDE results are system-dependent: low-rank DMD-assisted reconstructions improve Burgers and advection-diffusion discovery, while the raw baseline (without upsampling) remains competitive for the Fisher-KPP data. A comparison against linear and smoothing-spline interpolation techniques shows that the selected Koopman-based preprocessors provide overall performance gains over these non-dynamical alternatives. We also demonstrate that DMD-assisted upsampling can stabilize Pareto-based non-oracle support-size selection. Overall, Koopman-based upsampling is best viewed as a dynamics-aware preprocessing step that can reduce derivative-estimation error when its observable representation and low-rank structure are appropriate for the data.

papers.title: The Aldous property for normal Cayley graphs on symmetric groups
papers.summary: Aldous' spectral gap conjecture states that the random walk and the interchange process on any connected graph have the same spectral gap, or, equivalently, the second largest eigenvalue of any connected Cayley graph on the symmetric group $S_n$ with respect to a set of transpositions is achieved by the standard representation of $S_n$. This celebrated conjecture, proved in its general form in 2010, has inspired much interest in searching for other Cayley graphs on $S_n$ possessing this property, now known as the Aldous property. In this paper, we first prove that for $n \ge 5$ at most one of a normal Cayley graph on $S_n$ and its complement can possess the Aldous property except when these two graphs are $2K_{n!/2}$ and $K_{n!/2,n!/2}$ respectively. We then determine, for sufficiently large $n$, all normal Cayley graphs $\mathrm{Cay}(S_n, S)$ that have the Aldous property, except for the case when $S$ contains a permutation with support size in $\{2, 3, \dots, n-2\}$ and a permutation with support size in $\{n-1, n\}$, but not all permutations with support size $n$ are contained in $S$. In particular, we show that a non-complete normal Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(S_n, S)$ does not have the Aldous property if all permutations in $S$ have support size $n-1$ or $n$, or all permutations with support size $n$ are contained in $S$, thereby solving an open problem posed by Li, Xia and Zhou in 2023. Along the way we determine all normal Cayley graphs on $S_n$ that are line graphs, and classify all normal Cayley graphs on $S_n$ with the strictly second largest eigenvalue at most $1$.

papers.title: Minimal inversion of a permuton sample
papers.summary:
Given a permutation $σ$, its corresponding \textit{inversion graph} is obtained by adding an edge between $i<j$ if and only if $σ(i)>σ(j)$. The first results on random inversion graphs come from Acan and Pittel, who studied the connected threshold for a uniform permutation with fixed inversion number, and Bhattacharya and Mukherjee, who mostly focused on the degrees of the graph when the permutation is chosen uniformly at random.
  In this work, we call \textit{minimal inversion} the minimal degree of the inversion graph and extend a theorem from Bhattacharya and Mukherjee to the case where the permutation is not only uniform, but obtained as the ordering of points sampled according to some distribution on the plane. Under regularity assumptions on the distribution, and for the appropriate $α>0$, we show that the probability that the minimal inversion rescaled by $n^{α/(α+1)}$ is larger than $t$ behaves like $\exp(-ct^{α+1})$ for some constant $c>0$ depending on the distribution. We further show that every $α>0$ admits at least one corresponding distribution, thus proving that the minimal inversion can asymptotically scale as $n^β$ for any $β\in[0,1]$ (the cases $β=0$ and $β=1$ being obtained via the identity and anti-identity permutations, among others).

papers.title: Mining Verdict Boundaries for Neural Network Verification
papers.summary: Branch and Bound (BaB) aims to achieve complete verification of neural networks by adaptively partitioning the problem and applying off-the-shelf verifiers to subproblems. Its problem-splitting history can be represented as a tree, where each subproblem corresponds to a child node. A key problem of BaB lies in searching for the verdict boundaries across all the paths that divide the verified and unverified subproblems. We observe that the existing BaB approach tackles this problem by solving each expensive subproblem sequentially along the tree path as its depth increases, requiring costly bounds propagation at every visited BaB tree node (i.e., subproblem), which is inefficient. To address this issue, we propose effective search approaches that leverage the monotonicity of each path to efficiently and precisely locate the verdict boundary by simultaneously splitting multiple activation functions (e.g., ReLU), rather than processing them one at a time as in the classical approach. Our approach performs an effective exponential search along each path, allowing us to skip many boundary-unrelated subproblems when identifying the verdict boundary. The enhanced version further improves this process by estimating the boundary's position using quantitative information obtained from subproblem solving. We perform experimental evaluation on commonly-used benchmarks to assess our proposed techniques, and compare them with recent BaB-based approaches.

papers.title: Normalizers of lattices and isometry groups of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
papers.summary: We prove that every arithmetic lattice in PSL$(2,\mathbb{C})$ and every arithmetic lattice of the simplest type in PO$(n,1)$, $n\ge 2$, is the normalizer of arbitrarily many of its sublattices. Combined with previous work, this result implies that every lattice in PSL$(2,\mathbb{C})$ has this property. In this way, we prove that the set of profinitely flexible lattices in PSL$(2,\mathbb{C})$ is either empty or countably infinite. Another result is that every finite group is realized as the full isometry group of an arithmetic hyperbolic $n$-manifold. The proof of this theorem is based on study of normalizers of lattices and subgroup growth theory.

papers.title: Latent Lie-Poisson Neural Networks (LLPNNs): Discovering the motion of Lie-Poisson systems through observable data and latent dynamics
papers.summary:
Structure-preserving neural networks are essential for the long-term prediction of Hamiltonian systems from data. Many important Hamiltonian systems in mechanics and control admit symmetry reduction to Lie--Poisson systems, including rigid bodies, underwater vehicles, fluids, plasmas, and optimal control problems. A fundamental challenge in learning such systems is that their dynamics evolve in momentum variables that are typically unobservable, while available data consist only of observable quantities such as configurations and velocities. In optimal control applications, the situation is further complicated because the latent variables contain unobservable co-states and the Hamiltonian may be degenerate, preventing the existence of a corresponding Lagrangian and rendering the encoder-decoder approaches inapplicable.
  We introduce Latent Lie--Poisson Neural Networks (LLPNNs), a structure-preserving framework for learning Lie--Poisson dynamics directly from observable data. The proposed approach exploits three geometric ingredients: (i) learning either a Hamiltonian decoder or a pseudo-Lagrangian encoder on the active variables, (ii) constructing latent trajectories through a universal Noether invariant arising from Lie--Poisson symmetry reduction, and (iii) reconstructing observable and latent dynamics through Lie--Poisson flows combined with Magnus-based Lie-group updates. The resulting method preserves the geometric structure and is applicable to both regular and degenerate Hamiltonian systems.
  We demonstrate the method on three examples: a generalized rigid body on SO(3), Kirchhoff's underwater vehicle on SE(3), and an optimal-control problem for interacting vehicles on $SE(2)^N$. Numerical experiments show excellent long-term predictive accuracy, strong robustness to noise, and competitive performance using only modest datasets and lightweight neural-network architectures.

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29681v1.title: 奇閉路のシャノン容量に対するLeanで検証された下界
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29681v1.summary: 本論文では、小さな奇閉路のシャノン容量に関する新たな下界を提示している。具体的には、C₇に対する3.258805369885…以上という値をはじめ、C₁₁、C₁₃、C₁₅、C₁₉、C₂₁、C₂₃の各奇閉路について従来よりも精密な下界を導出した。これらの境界値は、Gao (2026) および Itty, Rosin, Carstensen and Reichman (2026) の手法に基づく反復的手順によって得られたものであり、その計算過程および結果は対話型定理証明支援系Leanによって完全に形式化・検証されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29681v1.appendix: 本論文は、組合せ論的なグラフ理論の課題であるシャノン容量を扱っており、[興味ある分野]のうち validated numerics (精度保証付き数値計算) の文脈、あるいは形式検証を通じた計算結果の正当性確保という観点で関連性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29612v1.title: 格子道、パターン統計、および Riordan 配列
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29612v1.summary: 彩色されたステップを持つ格子道に関連する新しい Riordan 行列のクラスを提案している。この行列のクラスが pseudo-involution の性質を持つことを示し、行列の各成分に対する生成関数および組合せ論的な明示式を導出した。さらに、これらの行列を用いて格子道内における任意のパターンの出現統計を計算する手法を確立している。最後に、格子道集合上に分配束の構造を定義し、得られた行列と束の Whitney 数との関係性を明らかにしている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29612v1.appendix: 本論文は格子道におけるパターンの統計を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち「combinatorics on words」や「symbolic dynamics」に関連する内容を含んでいます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29571v1.title: 完全群による拡大に対する強収束ユニタリ表現
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29571v1.summary: 本論文では、完全群（exact groups）による拡大から生じる可算群の様々な新しい設定において、強収束ユニタリ表現が存在することを証明している。具体的には、アメナブル群との半直積、アーベル群を基底とする一般化リース積、グラフリース積、Gersten群を含む様々なfree-by-cyclic群、およびC*-環上の一般的なベルヌーイ・シフト交叉積における存在を示している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29571v1.appendix: 本論文は可算無限群の表現論的性質を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち「structure of large countable infinite group」に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29496v1.title: Transcript-Managed Transformers: 単調なマルチエージェントの崩壊と2つのPop可能なTranscriptによる普遍性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29496v1.summary: 本論文は、有限精度の因果的TransformerにおけるTranscript管理の計算能力を数理的に分析しています。Transcriptを複数のチャンネルに分割し、ブロックの追加（Push）と直近ブロックの削除（Pop）を許容する「Transcript-Managed Transducer (TMT)」を定義しました。Pop操作を持たない標準的な追加専用のモデル（RTMT）は、エージェントの数に関わらず決定性有限状態変換（DFT）の範疇に限定されますが、Pop操作を導入することで計算能力が飛躍的に向上します。具体的には、1つのPop可能チャンネルで決定性文脈自由言語（DCFL）を、2つ以上のチャンネル（単一エージェントまたは複数エージェント間）で帰納的可算集合（RE）を表現可能であり、チューリング完全な計算能力（Universality）を持つことを示しました。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29496v1.appendix: 本論文はオートマトン理論 (automata theory) および形式言語理論 (formal languages) に深く関連しており、Transformerのアーキテクチャが持つ計算上の制約と、スタック構造を用いた計算能力の階層（DCFLやRE）へのマッピングを論じています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29449v1.title: Grigorchuk-Erschler群のBasilica群
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29449v1.summary: FrancoeurとGarridoは、無限指数の極大部分群を持つ有限生成ブランチ群の初の具体例としてGrigorchuk-Erschler群を提示した。本研究では、PetschickとRajeevが導入したBasilica演算を利用し、Grigorchuk-Erschler群の第2Basilica群も同様に無限指数の極大部分群を持つことを証明している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29449v1.appendix: 本論文は「structure of large countable infinite group」の分野に関連しており、有限生成ブランチ群の極大部分群の構造という重要なテーマを扱っています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29386v1.title: 有理ヤコビ回転と混合整数二次計画法の近似の計算複雑性
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29386v1.summary: 整数変数の数および目的関数のヘッセ行列における負の固有値の数が固定されている設定において、混合整数二次計画法（MIQP）のε-近似解を多項式時間で計算するアルゴリズムを提案しています。P≠NPを仮定すると、これらの制約は近似を効率的に行うために不可欠であり、これによりMIQP近似の計算複雑性が完全に特徴付けられました。技術的な核は、無理数演算を回避し、チューリングマシン上で実行可能な「有理ヤコビ回転」を用いた同時対角化手法です。これによって、楕円体を球体へ写像しつつ、目的関数を微小な摂動を除いて分離可能に変換します。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29386v1.appendix: 本論文は「興味ある分野」として挙げられた項目に直接関連するものではありませんが、計算複雑性理論および数理最適化における重要な成果です。特に、実数演算ではなくチューリングマシン上での演算可能性を保証するために有理数のみを用いた「有理ヤコビ回転」を導入している点は、精度保証付き数値計算（validated numerics）の基礎的な関心事である計算の厳密性とも親和性があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29369v1.title: ポリオミノによるタイリングの自動列挙
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29369v1.summary: 本論文では、ポリオミノによるタイリングを列挙するためのZeilbergerによる計算フレームワークを再検討し、回転を許容したL-テトロミノによるk × nボードのタイリングの計数への適用を実証している。BělohoubekとSlavíkによって最近示された2n × 4ボードのL-テトロミノ・タイリングの母関数を自動的に復元することで手法の検証を行い、さらにこの手法を幅5から9までのボードに適用した。その結果、陽な形での有理母関数を得ることに成功し、OEIS（オンライン整数列大辞典）に未登録の新しい整数列を導出した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29369v1.appendix: この論文は、タイリングの数え上げや母関数の導出を扱っており、興味ある分野のうち combinatorics on words と密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29326v1.title: マンデルブロ集合の先端における精緻な漸近挙動
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29326v1.summary: 二次写像 f_c(z) = z² + c において、ジュリア集合 J_c のハウスドルフ次元が1となるのは c = 0 と c = -2 のみである。本論文では、非双曲的なパラメータであるマンデルブロ集合の先端 c = -2 付近における次元関数の不連続な振る舞いを解析し、その下包絡線に対する鋭い一次の漸近評価を導出した。具体的には、c ∈ M のとき dim_H(J_c) が漸近的に 1 + Ω√|c + 2| 以上になることを示した（ここで Ω = √(2/3) / (π log 2) は Jaksztas 定数）。この証明のために、退化するボックス写像（box mappings）の族に対する熱力学形式を構築し、指数関数的裾の性質を利用して圧力関数の制御を行っている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29326v1.appendix: 本論文は複素力学系（complex dynamics）の分野に関連しており、Yoccoz problem（アトラクターの展開）に対する具体的な数学的貢献を含んでいます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29275v1.title: 動的Möbius-Sarnak過程のスペクトル解析とMöbius関数の位相的エントロピーについて
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29275v1.summary: 本論文では、エントロピーとスペクトルにおける可算ルベーグ成分を関連付けるRokhlin-Sinaiの仕組みを拡張し、動的Möbius-Sarnak過程が可算ルベーグ成分を持つことを示しました。また、バナッハ空間上の全演算子に対してスペクトル測度の概念を拡張し、Möbiusフローの位相的エントロピーが 6/π² log 3 であることを無条件で証明しました。これらの結果から、Möbius関数の任意の準ジェネリック測度に対して、そのフローが可算ルベーグスペクトル成分を持つことが導かれ、スペクトルが特異な任意の位相力学系においてSarnakのMöbius直交性予想が成立することが示されました。さらに、Möbius関数のすべての潜在的なスペクトル測度がルベーグ測度に対して絶対連続であることも明らかにしています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29275v1.appendix: 本論文は、記号力学系 (symbolic dynamics) および算術力学系 (arithmetic dynamics) の分野に深く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29272v1.title: 時系列グラフにおけるロール彩色
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29272v1.summary: グラフのロール彩色（同じ色の頂点が、隣接頂点の色集合に関して同一の構成を持つような彩色）の概念を時系列グラフへと拡張する。時系列ロールは、現在の色や過去・現在の隣接関係の情報を捕捉するオートマトンを用いて定義される。静的グラフにおける問題からの帰着により、時系列ロール彩色問題がNP完全であることを示した。計算の困難性に対処するため、オートマトンの状態数とグラフの幅尺度（vertex-interval-membership widthやtree-interval-membership width）を組み合わせたパラメータや、基礎グラフの木幅・生存期間・色数を組み合わせたパラメータにおいて、問題が固定パラメータ可能（FPT）であることを証明した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29272v1.appendix: 時系列ロールがオートマトンを用いて定義されており、解析においてもオートマトンの状態数がパラメータとして扱われていることから、「automata theory」に深く関連する内容です。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29255v1.title: 新たな有効なジャグリング・シーケンスに関する2つの結果について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29255v1.summary: 本論文では、ジャグリングの数理モデルであるサイトスワップ（siteswap）シーケンスを拡張するための2つの簡潔な操作、「first throws」と「last catches」について研究している。これらの構成法は、既存のパターンに対して衝突を発生させずに開始時に投げを追加したり、終了時にキャッチを追加したりするための手法である。着地時間（landing times）および置換テスト（permutation test）を用いることで、任意の有効なサイトスワップに対してこれらの操作を適用した際に、再び有効なサイトスワップが生成されるための必要十分条件を明らかにした。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29255v1.appendix: 本論文はジャグリングパターンの組合せ論的性質を扱っており、「combinatorics on words」や「symbolic dynamics」の分野と関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29236v1.title: 三角形面を最大化する擬直線配置の列挙と分類
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29236v1.summary: n本の擬直線（nは奇数）から成る単純な配置において、三角形面の数を最大化する配置を網羅的に列挙・分類するアルゴリズムを提案した。この手法は、最長置換 w₀ の簡約語を深さ優先探索で列挙する際、幾何学的制約に基づき偶数インデックスの生成元のみを分岐させる枝刈りを行う。得られた配置は、交換関係、ユークリッド変換、および射影変換の同値類によって階層的に分類され、完全な対称群や軌道・固定部分群のプロファイルが特定される。n=27までの完全な列挙（56,646の射影クラスなど）に加え、n=93までの部分的な探索結果を報告しており、探索の完全性も証明されている。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29236v1.appendix: 本論文は、word上の組合せ論（combinatorics on words）における最長置換の簡約語（reduced words）の表現や、幾何学的な配置の組合せ構造を扱っており、興味ある分野の「combinatorics on words」と強く関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29233v1.title: 高次元記号力学：3-graphのためのテキスタイル・フレームワーク
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29233v1.summary: 本論文では、2次元の有限型シフトのモデル化で知られるテキスタイル・システムを3次元へと拡張し、3-graphとの関連性を調査している。左分解的なテキスタイル・システムが2-graphのKumjian-Pask代数と一致するという既存の性質を拡張し、3次元テキスタイル・システムがすべての3次元有限型シフトを捉え、かつ3-graphの構造（3彩色グラフから3-graphを構成する際の結合律を含む条件など）を単純なプルバック図として記述できることを示した。さらに、3次元テキスタイルのホモロジー群を定義し、それが対応する3-graphのホモロジー群と一致することを証明することで、構築したフレームワークのホモロジー的な整合性を立証している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29233v1.appendix: 本論文は記号力学（symbolic dynamics）における多次元の有限型シフトを扱っており、興味ある分野と密接に関連しています。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29111v1.title: Fittingの定理と正規部分群の半環
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29111v1.summary: 群 G の正規部分群の集合に対して、非単位的かつ一般には非結合的な、可換半環の構造を定義しました。この視点を用いることで、2つのベキ零正規部分群の結びはベキ零であるというFittingの古典的な定理を、環論的な用語で再構成することができます。このアプローチにおける重要な要素は、非結合的な設定での二項展開と、2つの正規部分群の交換子群が各因子に含まれるという事実です。本研究はLeanで形式化されており、主要な定義や結果にはMathlibが活用されています。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29111v1.appendix: 本論文は群論的な構造を扱っていますが、指定された「興味ある分野」との直接的な関連性は特に認められません。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29105v1.title: N-素数グラフ問題は素数グラフ問題と同等である
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29105v1.summary: 有限群 G の整数群環における正規化単元群 V(ℤG) についての研究。V(ℤG) のすべての N-素数アークは、G 内に既に存在するか、あるいは異なる素数位数の可換な証拠を持つかのいずれかであることを証明した。これにより、V(ℤG) の N-素数グラフ A(Γ_N(V(ℤG))) を A(Γ_N(G)) と Γ_GK(V(ℤG)) の辺の対称化の和として表す公式を導出し、結果として N-素数グラフ問題が G に対して肯定的に解決されることと、素数グラフ問題が肯定的に解決されることが同値であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29105v1.appendix: 群環の単元群の構造に関連する研究であり、有限群の代数的構造を扱っています。提示された「興味ある分野」に直接合致するキーワードは含まれていませんが、群の構造論という観点から関連性を持ちます。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28992v1.title: Permuton標本における最小転倒数について
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28992v1.summary: 置換から生成される転倒グラフの最小次数（最小転倒数）に関する研究である。一様置換における先行研究を拡張し、平面上の特定の分布（Permuton）からサンプリングされた点集合の順序として得られる置換を対象としている。分布に対する正則性の仮定のもと、適切にスケーリングされた最小転倒数が特定の閾値を超える確率が指数関数的に減衰することを示した。また、任意のβ∈[0,1]に対して、最小転倒数が漸近的にn^βのオーダーでスケールするような分布が存在することを証明している。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28992v1.appendix: この論文は、置換やグラフの構造を扱うため、興味ある分野のうち「combinatorics on words」や離散構造の漸近的性質に関連があります。

http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28949v1.title: 算術的双曲多様体の等長写像群と格子の正規化群
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28949v1.summary: 本論文では、PSL(2, ℂ) のすべての算術的格子および PO(n, 1) (n ≥ 2) における最も単純な型のすべての算術的格子が、自身の任意に多くの部分格子の正規化群となることを証明した。先行研究と組み合わせることで、PSL(2, ℂ) 内のすべての格子がこの性質を持つことが導かれ、PSL(2, ℂ) における profinitely flexible な格子の集合が、空であるか、さもなくば可算無限集合であることが示される。さらに、格子の正規化群の研究と部分群増加理論に基づき、すべての有限群がある算術的双曲 n-次元多様体の完全等長写像群として実現可能であることを示した。
http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28949v1.appendix: 本論文は、格子の構造や正規化群を扱っており「structure of large countable infinite group」の分野に深く関連しています。

papers.title: Asymptotically optimal bracketing covers for anchored boxes
papers.summary:
Bracketing covers and $δ$-covers provide finite discretizations of the anchored boxes that define the star discrepancy. Let $N_{[]}(d,δ)$ and $N(d,δ)$ denote the corresponding bracketing and covering numbers. We prove the lower bounds \[
  N_{[]}(d,δ)\ge \lceil δ^{-d}\rceil,
  \qquad
  N(d,δ)\ge
  \left\lceil \frac{d!}{d^d}\,δ^{-d}\right\rceil. \] We also construct, for every fixed $d$, bracketing covers which, together with the lower bound, show that $N_{[]}(d,δ)=(1+o_d(1))δ^{-d}$ as $δ\downarrow0$. The construction combines a coarse partition with box-dependent anisotropic local grids. Its shared vertices yield $δ$-covers with asymptotic upper coefficient one. Explicit upper bounds are obtained for both quantities.

papers.title: Collinear Interior Lattice Points in Triangles Satisfying $B(T)\in\{4,5\}$
papers.summary: A positive integer $k$ is called $Bn$-collinear if at least one lattice triangle with $n$ boundary points ($B(T)=n$) and $k$ interior lattice points exists, and every such triangle has all of its interior points collinear. Building on prior work on $B(T)=3$, we completely classify the $B4$- and $B5$-collinear integers. Using canonical lattice classifications together with arithmetic properties of Alder's generalized totient function $g(k)$, we prove that the only $B4$-collinear integers are $k\in\{1,2,5\}$. Furthermore, we show that no integer is $B5$-collinear. This establishes a structural contrast: while three and four boundary lattice points exhibit some collinearity constraints, five boundary points disrupt the pattern.

papers.title: Assuming You Knew: Fixing an Epistemic Semantics for Flow Policies Using Agentic AI
papers.summary: Many high-level security requirements are about the allowed flow of information in programs and are difficult to make precise because they involve selective downgrading. Notions from epistemic logic have emerged as a good approach to policy semantics but a robust general framework remains elusive. A paper appearing in CSF 2018, entitled ``Assuming You Know: Epistemic Semantics of Relational Annotations for Expressive Flow Policies'', attempted to provide a unifying framework---but the formalization was sketchy and a correction was announced during the conference presentation. With aid from an agentic AI coding assistant, a corrected formalization has been machine checked in the Rocq proof assistant. The simplicity and generality of the framework may help compare different policy specification styles and enforce them by leveraging existing techniques.

papers.title: Intersecting families of sets are usually trivial for $n\ge 2k+3$
papers.summary: A family of subsets of $[n]$ is called intersecting if it contains no pair of disjoint sets. It is called trivial if all its members contain a common element. Frankl and Kupavskii, and independently Balogh, Das, Liu, Sharifzadeh, and Tran, proved that there is a constant $c>0$ such that, whenever $n \geq 2k+2+c\sqrt{k\ln k}$, almost all $k$-uniform intersecting families are trivial. Balogh, Garcia, Li, and Wagner later improved this range to $n \geq 2k+100\ln k$. In this paper, we prove that the same conclusion holds for every $n\geq 2k+3$. This verifies the conjectured conclusion of Balogh, Garcia, Li, and Wagner throughout this range.

papers.title: Block Sensitivity can exceed Spectral Sensitivity Squared
papers.summary: The spectral sensitivity $λ(f)$ of a Boolean function is the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of its sensitivity graph. It lower-bounds every standard measure of query complexity, and Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal, who introduced it, asked whether block sensitivity is at most quadratic in it: is $bs(f)=O(λ(f)^{2})$? We show that it is not. We construct a total Boolean function on $2017584$ variables with $bs(f)\ge 14011$ and $λ(f)\le 89.0162$, so that $bs(f)\geλ(f)^{2.127}$, and hence by composition a family with $λ(f_n)\to\infty$ and $bs(f_n)=Ω(λ(f_n)^{2.127})$. The function is the indicator of a union of $k$ subcubes indexed by the vertices of a doubly regular tournament, and the freedom left in the construction is fixed by the Lovász local lemma. The main result has been formally verified in Lean. We also give numerical evidence that a member of the same family on $1255$ variables reaches an exponent near $2.20$, and exhibit a member on $30$ variables whose exponent already exceeds $2$ and whose spectral sensitivity can be computed exactly.

papers.title: Small $q$-kernels in digraphs
papers.summary: We address three questions of Spiro [Europ. J. Combin., 133:Paper No. 104307, 2026] on smallest $q$-kernels in digraphs. All three questions are on the existence of small $q$-kernels in digraphs, where 'smallness' is measured in different ways. We answer one of these questions in the affirmative, and the other two in the negative. We further study the latter two questions in the context of bipartite digraphs. In particular, we show that in the bipartite setting, the answer to one of the two questions is affirmative if and only if $q$ is odd. For the other question, we show that the answer is positive when the digraph is bipartite and $q$ is odd (the case when the digraph is bipartite and $q$ is even remains open).

papers.title: Weakly Normally Hyperbolic Invariant Tori: Persistence and an Averaging Principle
papers.summary: We prove a persistence theorem for attracting weakly normally hyperbolic invariant tori under small time-periodic perturbations. The theorem extends recent continuation results for weakly normally hyperbolic limit cycles to invariant tori of arbitrary dimension, providing a general analytical framework for their detection. As an application, we establish an averaging principle showing that attracting normally hyperbolic invariant $d$-tori of the averaged system give rise to attracting normally hyperbolic invariant $(d+1)$-tori of the original non-autonomous system. We further introduce a polynomiality-preserving construction that simultaneously lifts the dimensions of the phase space and the attracting normally hyperbolic invariant tori, yielding recursive lower bounds for the maximal number of codimension-$1$ normally hyperbolic invariant tori of polynomial vector fields of a given degree, thereby extending the counting aspect of Hilbert's sixteenth problem to higher-dimensional invariant tori. In particular, we prove that this number grows at least polynomially with the degree and becomes unbounded for invariant tori of higher codimension.

papers.title: Odd-Girth Bounds for Defective Edge Coloring
papers.summary: A $(k,d)$-edge coloring of a loopless multigraph $G$ is an edge coloring using at most $k$ colors such that the subgraph formed by each color class has maximum degree at most $d$. The least such $k$ is denoted by $χ'_d(G)$. Let $G$ be a loopless non-bipartite multigraph with maximum degree $Δ(G)$ and odd girth $g_0(G)$, and let $d\ge1$ be odd. We prove that \[ χ'_d(G)\le\left\lceil\frac{g_0(G)Δ(G)-1}{dg_0(G)-1}\right\rceil. \] For $d=1$, this is Goldberg's odd-girth refinement of Shannon's theorem, while for $g_0(G)=3$ it is the defective Shannon bound of Aboulker, Aubian, and Huang. For every odd $d>1$, every odd $g_0\ge3$, and every $Δ>d$, an almost full ring multigraph $R(Δ,g_0)$, an odd cycle with edge multiplicities alternating between $\lfloorΔ/2\rfloor$ and $\lceilΔ/2\rceil$, except that two consecutive edges have multiplicity $\lfloorΔ/2\rfloor$, attains equality. We also derive a range in which the defective Goldberg--Seymour conjecture holds.

papers.title: Taming the Search Space: Solving and Generating Hitori and Binairo Puzzles
papers.summary: This paper investigates solving and generation techniques for the logic puzzles Hitori and Binairo. Two solving paradigms are compared: backtracking with domain-specific optimizations, and SAT-based solving via conjunctive normal form encodings. An empirical evaluation analyzes runtime, explored search nodes, and branching factor across varying puzzle sizes. To support systematic benchmarking in the evaluation, generators capable of producing valid and uniquely solvable puzzle instances are developed. Results indicate that constraint propagation is the most effective backtracking optimization, substantially reducing the effective branching factor, search tree size, and thus runtime. Heuristic variable ordering and scoring strategies provide additional improvements. For Binairo, the SAT-based approach solves all evaluated instances within low runtime, while optimized backtracking fails to solve difficult puzzle instances within the timeout. For Hitori, propagation-based backtracking achieves the best results, while for the SAT-based approach the iterative connectivity check takes up the majority of the runtime, failing difficult puzzle instances.

papers.title: Uniform expansion in finite groups of Lie type
papers.summary: We prove that finite simple groups $G(p)$ of bounded rank and with $p$ prime have uniform expansion, that is, the family of all the Cayley graphs forms a family of (two-sided) expanders, except perhaps when $p$ belongs to a small family of exceptional primes. Furthermore, for all prime powers $q$, the set of possible exceptions to uniform expansion of $G(q)$ is shown to have ``dimension zero''. We also extend these results to semisimple and perfect algebraic groups.

papers.title: Parking Cascades: From the Simplest Sequence to Motzkin and Catalan
papers.summary: We introduce $k$-cascading parking functions, a parametrized variant of parking functions in which cars form bumping cascades of up to $k \geq 0$ cars. Setting $k = 0$ recovers classical parking functions, whereas $k = 1$ recovers MVP parking functions. Although parking functions and cascading parking functions are equivalent as sets, they are generally distinct as maps. Therefore, in this paper we consider the enumeration of the fibers of their outcomes. Our main result is a recursive, permutation pattern-based formula for the size of the fiber of any given permutation, for any given $k \geq 0$. When specialized to the longest word, the formula reduces to a family of integer sequences that interpolate between the simplest sequence ($k=0$), the Motzkin numbers ($k = 1$), and the Catalan numbers ($k\geq n-1$). When specialized to the set of layered permutations, the formula gives new combinatorial interpretations for the row sums of certain convolution triangles, including Motzkin and Catalan convolution triangles.

papers.title: Poisson approximations of the number of fixed points in random multiset permutations
papers.summary: For ordinary permutations on $n$ letters, the distribution of the number of fixed points of a random permutation is well known to approach the Poisson$(1)$ distribution in total variation distance as $n\to\infty$. We use Stein's method to get related results for the number of fixed points of random permutations of multisets.

papers.title: Alternating Groups and Embeddings into Groups Invariably Generated by Two Prime-Order Elements
papers.summary: For any distinct primes $p$ and $q$, we prove that there is a finite group which does not embed into any finite group invariably generated by an element of order $p$ and an element of order $q$. This gives a negative answer to Problem 21.142 of the Kourovka Notebook \cite{kourovka21}. In fact, for every fixed pair $p,q$, the group $A_n$ cannot embed into such a group once $n$ is sufficiently large in terms of $p$ and $q$.

papers.title: Odd-Cycle Span Defect: A Polynomial Lower Bound and a Square-Root Upper Bound
papers.summary: For a graph $G$, let $ψ(G)=\max\{χ(G[V(C)]):C$ is an odd cycle of $G\}$, with $ψ(G)=0$ when $G$ is bipartite. For positive integers $N$, set $F(N)=\max\{χ(G)-ψ(G):|V(G)|\le N\}$. The function $F$ measures the finite-order additive gap arising from an open problem of Erdos and Hajnal. We prove $N^{1/6-o(1)}\le F(N)<\sqrt{6N}$. The lower bound raises the finite-order scale supplied by the Cameron-Clow path-colour construction from $\log N/\log\log N$ to a fixed power of $N$. Its proof constructs a palette-code graph from a binary covering code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq\{0,1\}^p$ and establishes the exact identities $χ(G)=2p+\ell-ρ(\mathcal{C})$ and $ψ(G)=2p$. Near-middle Hamming coverings yield the exponent $1/6$. The upper bound combines Polavarapu's connectivity theorem, the Chvatal-Erdos Hamiltonicity theorem, and maximum-independent-set stripping.

papers.title: Compact SAT and MaxSAT Encodings for Business-to-Business Meeting Scheduling with Idle-Time Balancing
papers.summary: Business-to-business meeting scheduling assigns requested pairwise meetings to time slots and locations under availability, capacity, conflict, and precedence constraints. The published Boolean formulation retains meeting-slot assignments that propagation can eliminate and encodes precedence relations with pairwise clauses. We present compact SAT and MaxSAT encodings based on solution-preserving domain filtering, variables shared at selected precedence boundaries, and an objective that minimizes the range of participants' internal idle-slot totals. Experiments on 126 official and 100 higher-density derived instances examine domain filtering, precedence representation, transitive relations, and optimization method. Compared with an adapted published MaxSAT formulation using the same objective, the proposed encoding reduces the median clause count by 40.3% and median peak memory usage by 55.9%. Domain filtering alone reduces assignment variables by 24.1% and clauses by 16.2%. Sharing variables at selected precedence boundaries reduces clauses by 0.5%-1.0% on official precedence instances and by up to 5.5% at the highest derived density. The idle-time measure distinguishes one-slot interruptions from longer waits, while aggregate idle time provides a complementary measure. Compared with Gurobi, a leading commercial solver, all three SAT and MaxSAT methods solve every official instance with lower median total times.

papers.title: Dynamics on graphs with disjoint cycles and applications
papers.summary: In this article, we introduce the notion of connected finite graphs with disjoint cycles in normal form and show that any such graph can be transformed into a normal form graph via a finite sequence of in-splittings and out-splittings. Consequently, we provide number-theoretic criteria for meteor graphs of length three to be strongly shift equivalent, where a meteor graph of length three is a connected finite essential graph consisting of three disjoint cycles which makes a unique chain of cycles of length three. We then prove that meteor graphs of length three whose cycle lengths are pairwise coprime are shift equivalent if and only if they are strongly shift equivalent, if and only if their corresponding Leavitt path algebras are graded Morita equivalent, if and only if their graded $K$-theories, $K^{gr}_0$, are $\mathbb{Z}[x, x^{-1}]$-module isomorphic.
